The birth weight was 4110 grams, and there were no complications at delivery. The newborn had a routine physical exam with all systems within normal limits. clinicalSummary.chief_complaint: Yearly exam, YEARLY EXAM AND PAP
clinicalSummary.clinical_context: The patient is a 38-year-old female who presented for a routine yearly gynecological examination. She has no current concerns or new health changes. Her gynecological history includes a history of abnormal pap smears and high-risk HPV. She has a history of cryosurgery for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia. The physical examination was unremarkable, and a Pap smear and clinical breast examination were performed. The patient was educated on contraception, mammograms, and breast self-examination. She is scheduled to return in one year.
secondary_diagnoses: History of high-risk human papillomavirus (HR HPV)
History of cryosurgery for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia (CKC)
History of allergies to cefaclor and sulfa (sulfonamide antibiotics)

clinicalSummary.clinical_context: The patient is a 22-year-old female at 37 weeks gestation with a chief complaint of pregnancy. She has been experiencing right leg swelling and pain, for which a Doppler ultrasound was ordered to rule out DVT. The patient is O positive, rubella immune, and has a history of T12, L1 fracture. She prefers nitrous oxide and IV pain medication for labor and delivery, avoiding an epidural due to her back history. The patient is scheduled to return to the office in 1 week for a follow-up.
